_comment: Hindi profile. Voices for hi-IN: kiara (feminine), arjun (masculine). Nova 2 Sonic also supports SYSTEM_SPEECH content to control Latin/Devanagari transcription for code-switching; this profile leaves transcription at the model default.
_localeComment: BCP-47 codes for Amazon Transcribe, which gives the coaching lane an independent transcript and identifies which language was actually spoken. Streaming identification needs at least two options, one dialect each.
_espeakComment: espeak-ng voice used to phonemise the transcript into EXPECTED phonemes. It must match the language being taught: phonemising English text with the Spanish voice turns "Hello" into "e ʎ o", which makes the comparison against what Wav2Vec2 actually heard meaningless.
_genderComment: Must match the voice: gendered languages conjugate self-reference. Feminine voices: tiffany, amy, olivia, kiara, ambre, beatrice, tina, lupe, carolina. Masculine: matthew, arjun, florian, lorenzo, lennart, carlos, leo.
clarifyPhrase: क्या? मुझे ठीक से सुनाई नहीं दिया
regionalVariation: English loanwords mixed mid-sentence, which is ordinary everyday Hindi and not an error
Urdu-influenced vocabulary along with the q, kh and gh sounds
schwa dropped at the end of words
regional differences in how retroflex consonants are articulated
_learnerErrorsComment: The other side of the coin from regionalVariation: mistakes learners genuinely make that must NOT be excused as accent. Without these the reviewer treats almost everything as dialect and stays silent.
learnerErrors: replacing retroflex consonants (ट, ड) with English alveolar t and d
dropping aspiration where it distinguishes words (कल / खल)
flattening the दंत्य dental t and d into English ones
ignoring vowel length where it changes the word
pronunciationExample: your "ट" in "टमाटर" came out like an English "t", which makes it sound like a different word
grammarExample: "मैंने खाना खाया" — a completed action puts ने on the subject
